faqs.q: How do I book a driving lesson?
faqs.a: Complete the enquiry form on this page or call or text 07738 022010. Tell us your experience, preferred lesson times and the type of driving tuition you need, and we’ll help you with the next step. Do you teach complete beginners?

Yes. Beginner driving lessons are structured around your individual pace, starting with essential vehicle controls, observations and basic road skills before progressing to more complex driving situations. Do you offer intensive driving lessons?

faqs.q: Do you offer intensive driving lessons?
faqs.a: Yes. Intensive driving tuition can be arranged based on your current driving ability, availability and test goals. Contact us to discuss the most suitable option. Frequently Asked Questions

faqs.q: Do you offer both manual and automatic driving lessons?
faqs.a: We offer flexible packages including weekly sessions, weekend blocks, and intensive training programs. Our packages are designed to fit your schedule and budget. Can you help nervous drivers?

Yes. Nervous-driver lessons are available for learners who feel anxious, lack confidence or have had a difficult previous learning experience. Lessons are calm, patient and adapted to your confidence level. Can you help if I already have a practical test booked?

faqs.q: Can you help if I already have a practical test booked?
faqs.a: Yes. If you already have a test date, include it in your enquiry. We can discuss your current driving standard, available preparation time and whether focused test preparation or mock driving tests would be appropriate. What areas do you cover?

Mancunian Driving School provides driving lessons across Manchester and surrounding areas by arrangement. Include your postcode in your enquiry and we’ll confirm availability. Do you offer refresher lessons for full licence holders?

faqs.q: Do you offer refresher lessons for full licence holders?
faqs.a: Yes. Refresher driving lessons are available for qualified drivers who want to rebuild confidence, return to driving after a break or improve specific skills.

Begin Your Driving Journey With Confidence Your first lessons should feel organised, understandable and encouraging. Learn the controls, observations, positioning and decision-making skills you need at a pace that works for you.

Turn Your Driving Skills Into Test-Day Confidence Refine your independent driving, practise challenging situations and identify weaknesses before test day with structured preparation and realistic mock-test practice.

Whether you are looking for your first driving lesson, changing instructors, returning to driving or preparing for an upcoming practical test, tell us what you need and we will help you find the right training option. We aim to respond to lesson enquiries within 24 hours. Phone: 07738 022010

faqs.q: Should I choose manual or automatic driving lessons?
faqs.a: Manual tuition may suit learners who want the flexibility to drive both manual and automatic cars after qualifying with a manual licence. Automatic lessons can suit learners who prefer to concentrate on road awareness and decision-making without managing a clutch and manual gear changes. Can I change from pay as you go to a block booking?

faqs.q: Can I change from pay as you go to a block booking?
faqs.a: Contact Mancunian Driving School to discuss your current training and available package options. We can help you choose the lesson arrangement that best suits your progress and schedule. Payments & Lesson Packages

faqs.q: Can complete beginners book these lessons?
faqs.a: Yes. Both lesson formats can be tailored to beginners. Training starts with the fundamentals before progressing into more complex road situations as your skills and confidence develop. Do you offer evening and weekend driving lessons?

faqs.q: Do you offer evening and weekend driving lessons?
faqs.a: Yes. Mancunian Driving School currently advertises morning, evening and weekend lessons, subject to instructor availability.

faqs.q: Ready to Feel More Confident Behind the Wheel ?
faqs.a: You do not need to arrive at your first lesson already feeling confident. That is what good training is there to build. Whether you're a complete beginner, returning after a break, changing instructors or preparing for an upcoming practical test, Faz will help you understand what to work on and move forward with a clear plan. Start learning with a Manchester driving school that treats you as an individual rather than another name on the timetable.

Learning to drive is about much more than memorising manoeuvres or preparing for a test. Faz takes a calm, structured and learner-focused approach designed to help you understand why you are doing something, not simply what to do.

Having originally trained through BSM before continuing independently, Faz has built Mancunian Driving School around patient instruction, clear communication and lessons adapted to the individual. Learners are encouraged to develop each core driving skill properly before moving on to more demanding roads, junctions, manoeuvres and test preparation .

Visual learning is also an important part of Faz’s approach. Where useful, road layouts, manoeuvres and difficult traffic situations can be broken down using diagrams, videos and iPad-based explanations , helping learners understand situations before putting them into practice on the road.

Mancunian Driving School has been helping learners throughout Manchester since 2011, with a straightforward philosophy: every learner is different, so every learner deserves training suited to their individual needs.

Rather than forcing every pupil through the same lesson plan, training is shaped around your existing experience, confidence, aspirations and timescale . Fundamental skills are developed first, then more complex situations are introduced as your competence grows.

The objective goes beyond simply getting you through the practical driving test. We want learners to leave their training able to make safe decisions independently and feel prepared for everyday driving after passing.

Effective driving lessons should help you understand road situations as well as experience them. Faz combines practical tuition with supporting tools and clear explanations to make difficult concepts easier to understand.

Your training can be structured around your experience, goals, availability and progress rather than following a rigid timetable.
We do not believe in unrealistic “guaranteed pass” claims. No instructor can honestly guarantee the outcome of a practical driving test.

What we can promise is professional tuition, clear explanations, honest feedback and a learning plan adapted to your progress — giving you the strongest possible foundation for test day and independent driving afterwards.
This is much stronger for trust than inventing a pass guarantee.

Learning successfully requires more than an instructor telling you when to turn or when to change gear. You need someone who understands your confidence level, identifies the reason behind recurring mistakes and gives you a clear path forward.

At Mancunian Driving School, lessons are designed to build understanding first and independence next . Skills are introduced progressively so you can develop safe habits rather than relying on constant prompts from your instructor.
We provide professional guidance for both learners and instructors, ensuring a smooth and safe driving experience.

Faz is the driving instructor at the heart of Mancunian Driving School. His approach is straightforward: understand the learner first, then teach in a way that makes driving easier to understand and easier to remember.

After beginning his instructor training through BSM, Faz went on to develop his own teaching style around real learner needs. Rather than rushing through topics, he focuses on helping pupils understand what is happening around them, why a decision matters and how to respond safely without depending on constant prompts.

Faz also understands that people absorb information differently. Practical demonstrations can be supported with visual explanations, road diagrams, videos and digital learning tools where they add value. This makes more difficult subjects such as junctions, positioning, manoeuvres and road planning easier to break down before putting them into practice.

His aim is not to produce learners who simply know a test route. It is to develop drivers who can think independently, recognise risk and make sensible decisions once the instructor is no longer sitting beside them.
